children: A longtime aide to Republican Texas Governor Greg Abbott who served as the state's interim attorney general during Ken Paxton's 2023 impeachment proceedings was confirmed by the US Senate on Wednesday as a federal judge.

The Republican-led Senate voted 50-47 to confirm Angela Colmenero, Abbott's deputy chief of staff, to the position of a life-tenured judge in Houston in the US District Court for the Southern District of Texas.

The vote came during a push by the White House to secure the confirmation of as many judges as possible before the year's end amid the looming risk that Democrats retake the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections.

President Donald Trump has secured the confirmation of 290 of his judicial nominees during his two terms, including three US Supreme Court justices, helping shift the judiciary's ideological balance to the right.
In nominating Colmenero to a judgeship, Trump in a May social media post hailed her for doing an "incredible job" as a top aide to Abbott and said she would "always protect our Great Constitution."

Colmenero, 47, began working under Abbott in 2009 when he was serving as the attorney general of Texas. After Abbott became governor in 2015, she remained in the attorney general's office under Paxton for three years while serving as the chief of its general litigation division.

During her time in the office, she defended a Republican-backed state law requiring photo identification at the ballot box and argued in favor of state redistricting plans facing Voting Rights Act challenges.

She also served as lead trial counsel in a lawsuit challenging President Barack Obama's executive action to defer deportation of certain immigrant children and parents who are in the country illegally.
She rejoined Abbott as an aide to the governor in 2018, initially as a deputy general counsel before rising to become deputy chief of staff in 2023.

In response to written questions from Senate Democrats, Colmenero said that while Abbott was governor, she advised on policies ranging from his banning of COVID-19 mask mandates to the busing of migrants to cities led by Democrats.

When Paxton was impeached by the Texas House of Representatives in May 2023 on allegations of corruption, Abbott appointed Colmenero as provisional attorney general, a role she held until the state Senate acquitted him that September.
Paxton is now the Republican candidate for a seat in the U.S. Senate.
